I commend our detectives, SWAT Team, and the U.S. Marshals Service for their commitment to this mission. We will continue to pursue those who traffic dangerous narcotics and do everything within our authority to make St. Lucie County the safest county in Florida.” Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25

hero.headline: Martin County approves limited-industrial zoning for Hobe Sound site despite data center concerns
hero.body:
Martin County commissioners approved limited-industrial zoning for property along Southeast Powerline Avenue in Hobe Sound on Tuesday in a 3-2 vote that stepped back from a general-industrial designation but left at least one commissioner with concerns about future data center development. The property owner accepted the less-intensive classification after nearby residents pushed back against the broader zoning proposal.

Commissioner Blake Capps voted against the rezoning, citing concerns about the potential for a data center on the site. "Who knows where this is really going in the future and to approve a zoning for this property that allows a data center. I'm not into that," Capps said. The county said there are no plans for a data center at the site. Any proposal exceeding 100,000 square feet would require board approval.

Residents who spoke at the Tuesday commission meeting said their primary concern was protecting the character of the community. "Our biggest concern was preserving our quality of life. We don't have a lot of industry and a lot of noise," said Steve Addison, who has lived in the area since 1969. Kim Call, a resident, said growth needs to be compatible with the existing community. Patrick McDonough, a Hobe Sound resident and Eaglewood Community HOA president, said residents were concerned about the permanence of a general-industrial classification. "We believe is too broad and too open-ended," McDonough said.

Bob Reins, a land-use attorney with Gunster law firm representing the property owner, told commissioners his client was willing to accept the limited-industrial classification. "To cooperate and show if that's what the neighbors feel is more appropriate and that would be a better use then we are willing to accept the light industrial," Reins said. The property has long been slated for some form of industrial use, but the county said the existing zoning was outdated and due for an update. Addison said he felt the compromise was a win for both sides. "I don't want to see over development, but I also don't want to be that guy that doesn't understand land-use and doesn't understand property rights," Addison said.

hero.headline: Vandrell Jacobs sentenced to 10 years for Vero Beach apartment shooting, high-speed chase
hero.teaser: A 25-year-old man will spend a decade in prison for firing bullets into a Vero Beach apartment occupied by a family and leading deputies on a dangerous high-speed pursuit.
hero.body:
Vandrell Jacobs, 25, has been sentenced to 10 years in prison for his role in a January 2024 shooting at the Orangewood Apartments in Vero Beach and the high-speed chase that followed, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office.

Deputies responded to reports of gunfire at the Orangewood Apartments on Jan. 28, 2024. Investigators said five bullets struck an apartment occupied by a family. Witnesses reported seeing people inside a red Mercedes firing shots toward an intended victim before fleeing the scene.

Surveillance footage shows the Mercedes stopping in the area of the shooting before driving away. Flock cameras recorded the car for about two minutes before the shooting occurred, according to the sheriff's office. A deputy who responded to the shooting pursued the Mercedes, but the car fled at a high speed and ran red lights.

The Mercedes was located the following day, and Jacobs was arrested on Jan. 29, 2024. At the time, he admitted to the allegations. Jacobs was charged with shooting into a dwelling, vehicle, or building and fleeing police with disregard for safety. He now begins his decade-long prison sentence.

hero.headline: Amendment 3 support at 45% in new poll, below threshold needed to pass
hero.body:
A new St. Pete Polls survey shows support for Amendment 3 at about 45%, well below the 60% threshold required for Florida constitutional amendments to pass, with roughly 30% opposed and nearly a quarter of voters undecided. The property tax measure would increase the homestead exemption for non-school property taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, and lower the annual assessment-growth cap for non-homestead properties from 10% to 5%.

Gov. Ron DeSantis is urging voters to approve the amendment despite acknowledging it falls short of the property-tax changes he wanted. DeSantis said voters should pass the measure or risk getting no relief on property tax. The proposal has the Florida Republican Party's endorsement, and Florida Realtors has committed $10 million to the campaign supporting it.

The Florida Sheriffs Association has launched an advertising campaign opposing the amendment, warning of consequences for public safety. Police and firefighter groups have joined the opposition, questioning how communities would replace revenue supporting emergency services. Jennifer Cook Pritt of the Florida Police Chiefs Association said at a press event this week that the measure provides no clear path to fund core public safety services. Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd described the situation as a train wreck.

A legislative analysis estimates the amendment would reduce local non-school property-tax revenue by approximately $4.95 billion in the 2027-28 fiscal year and $8.78 billion in 2028-29. Supporters argue the changes would help homeowners manage costs and that local governments can reduce spending without sacrificing essential services. The St. Pete Polls survey contacted 913 likely voters Sept. 15-17 and reported a margin of error of 3.2 percentage points. Voters will decide the amendment in November.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie road rage shooting suspect charged with attempted homicide
hero.body:
A road rage confrontation on Southwest Brevity Terrace in Port St. Lucie that escalated into a shooting Thursday evening has resulted in attempted homicide charges for the suspected shooter and burglary with assault or battery charges for the other man involved. Tylon Kukielka, 57, faces the attempted homicide charge after allegedly firing his gun and striking Dean Plotts, 41, twice in the left wrist and legs during a physical fight. Plotts was charged with burglary with assault or battery.

The incident happened at about 6:30 p.m. near Southwest California Boulevard and Southwest Brevity Terrace, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department. Before the shooting, one driver believed he was being followed after merging onto Southwest Crosstown Parkway. The vehicles had passed each other, and one driver believed the other had cut him off. Investigators determined there was no intentional following.

Kukielka was driving with his girlfriend to her home after leaving a local restaurant. Plotts was traveling in the same direction. The situation escalated into a physical fight near Southwest Brevity Terrace. During the fight, Kukielka allegedly fired his gun.

A St. Lucie County sheriff's deputy traveling in the area witnessed the incident and detained Kukielka. Plotts was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital for treatment. Kukielka was also taken to a hospital for a medical evaluation. Investigators recovered surveillance video and shell casings during the investigation. Both men were taken into custody. The incident remains under investigation.

hero.headline: Martin County issues blue-green algae alert for Lake Okeechobee at J&S Fish Camp after toxins detected
hero.body:
The Florida Department of Health in Martin County issued a blue-green algae health alert for the Lake Okeechobee NES135 area after water samples collected in September detected harmful toxins. The area is located on the north shore of the lake at J&S Fish Camp in Martin County.

Residents and visitors should not drink, swim, wade, use personal watercraft or otherwise come into contact with water where a visible algae bloom is present. Health officials advised people to keep pets and livestock away from affected water. Anyone who comes into contact with algae, discolored water or water with an unpleasant odor should wash their skin and clothing with soap and water.

Contaminated water should not be used for cooking or washing dishes because boiling does not remove algae toxins. Blue-green algae are bacteria commonly found in Florida freshwater. Blooms can discolor water and create floating mats, scum, foam or paint-like material on the surface, sometimes with an unpleasant odor. The blooms can produce toxins that may harm people, pets and aquatic life.

Children, older adults and people with weakened immune systems may be at risk even at low toxin concentrations and should avoid exposure. Health officials said it is safe to eat fillets from healthy freshwater fish caught in lakes experiencing blooms if the fillets are rinsed with tap or bottled water, the guts are discarded and the fish is thoroughly cooked. People should not eat shellfish from waters with algae blooms.

The Florida Department of Environmental Protection monitors reported blooms and collects samples for analysis. The public can report an algae bloom online at ReportAlgalBloom.com or call 1-855-305-3903. Anyone who develops symptoms after exposure to a harmful algae bloom can call the Florida Poison Information Center at 800-222-1222. Pet owners who believe an animal became ill after exposure should contact a veterinarian. For health questions about blue-green algae, call DOH-Martin at 772-221-4090.

hero.headline: DeSantis signs death warrant for man who killed Indian River County deputy in 1986
hero.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a death warrant Friday for William Reaves, convicted of killing Indian River County Deputy Sheriff Richard Raczkowski in 1986. Reaves is scheduled for execution by lethal injection at Florida State Prison in Starke on Oct. 20.

Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers has been pushing DeSantis to sign the warrant for Reaves, calling it a priority case. Flowers told WPEC last July that he was frustrated by the delay. "Ultimately it was decided a long time ago that he would face the death penalty, and it's time for him to actually face the consequences," Flowers said. "He's exhausted all of his appeals. Many other cases just like his have resulted in execution, and for some reason, he continues to cost us taxpayer dollars every single day."

According to court records, Reaves shot Raczkowski four times in the back outside a Zippy Mart convenience store near Vero Beach on Sept. 23, 1986. Reaves had called 911 from a pay phone because he didn't have money for a cab. Raczkowski, who was dispatched to the call, phoned the 911 dispatcher to order a cab for Reaves and to inquire about outstanding warrants. During this time, Reaves said a gun fell out of his pants. After Raczkowski attempted to block Reaves from retrieving the gun, a struggle ensued and Reaves wrestled the weapon away. The deputy asked Reaves not to kill him and turned to run away. Reaves then fired four times into Raczkowski's back. The deputy died a short time later.

Reaves went to the home of a friend, who later told police Reaves confessed to shooting the deputy, saying he was high on cocaine and panicked. Police arrested Reaves three days later at a bus stop and charged him with first-degree murder, possession of a firearm by a convicted felon and trafficking in cocaine. A jury found Reaves guilty of first-degree murder in September 1987 and unanimously recommended the death penalty. The Florida Supreme Court reversed the conviction and sentence in 1991, finding the trial court erred by allowing a prosecutor who had previously defended Reaves in a criminal matter. A second jury found Reaves guilty of first-degree murder in February 1992, voting 10-2 to recommend a death sentence.

Counsel for Reaves filed a motion Friday for a stay until pending motions regarding another condemned prisoner, William Lee Thompson, are resolved. Brittney Lacy, Reaves' attorney, stated both clients are due the best representation, particularly when both are facing scheduled execution dates. The warrant is DeSantis' 18th death warrant of the year. Florida has carried out 15 executions this year and 43 under DeSantis.

cards.headline: Sebastian police fatally shoot Keaton Daucher holding shotgun on Joy Haven Drive
cards.teaser: Interim Sebastian police Chief Tim Wood confirmed Friday that two officers fatally shot 41-year-old Keaton Daucher after he emerged from his home with a shotgun during a noise-complaint call Thursday night. The Florida Department of Law Enforcement is now investigating.
cards.body:
Two Sebastian police officers fatally shot 41-year-old Keaton Daucher after he came out of his home with a shotgun Thursday night in the 500 block of Joy Haven Drive, interim police Chief Tim Wood confirmed Friday morning. The officers arrived at about 9:25 p.m. for a noise complaint and have been placed on paid administrative leave.

Wood said officers made contact with Daucher's mother and could hear Daucher yelling inside the home while they were speaking with her. Daucher then came out of the home with a shotgun, prompting the two officers to discharge their weapons, killing him.

Police said it was unclear if Daucher, who lived at the home, pointed the shotgun at the officers or if he fired any shots. Neither of the officers were hurt.

The investigation has been turned over to the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, which is standard practice for the Sebastian Police Department. Police said law enforcement had previously been at the house before Thursday but did not specify how many times.

cards.headline: Indian River County sex sting nets 50 arrests, child-luring case highlighted
cards.teaser: Sheriff Eric Flowers announced more than 50 arrests from Operation Late Checkout, a four-day multi-agency operation that targeted human trafficking and illegal sexual activity in Indian River County. The operation also resulted in three ICE detainers and one arrest involving a man who traveled to meet a minor.
cards.body:
Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers announced Thursday that law enforcement made more than 50 arrests during a four-day operation called Operation Late Checkout that targeted human trafficking and illegal sexual activity in the county.

The operation ran from Sept. 13 and netted over 60 contacts, more than 50 arrests, and three ICE detainers, Flowers said during a press conference. Agencies involved included the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Florida Department of Law Enforcement, St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Seminole County Sheriff's Office, Altamonte Springs Police Department, Vero Beach Police Department, Homeland Security Investigations, Florida Office of Statewide Prosecutor and the U.S. Attorney's Office.

One case involved a man who traveled to Indian River County to meet a minor. Flowers said the arrest was the result of the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force working across agencies to apprehend individuals attempting to lure children online. Several victims were identified during the operation, and ongoing investigations are underway. Flowers said there are no specific arrests on human trafficking charges at this time.

Undercover teams were deployed in a variety of capacities during the operation. Victims' advocates trained to work with trafficking victims were on hand to speak with women involved in prostitution to determine whether they were being trafficked. Flowers called the operation unprecedented for Indian River County. FDLE Assistant Special Agent in Charge Alfonso Williams said Operation Late Checkout was initiated by FDLE in coordination with the Indian River County Sheriff's Office and is the first operation of this magnitude conducted in the county. Williams said the operation focused on identifying human trafficking victims, reducing the demand for prostitution, and apprehending individuals seeking sexual contact with minors. FDLE houses the Florida Trafficking Hotline at 1-855-352-7233 for anyone who suspects someone is a victim of trafficking.

hero.headline: Road rage shooting on SW Brevity Terrace leads to arrest of two Port St. Lucie men
hero.body:
A road rage confrontation on Southwest Brevity Terrace in Port St. Lucie escalated into a shooting Thursday evening that left one man wounded and two men facing criminal charges. Tylon Kukielka, 57, was charged with attempted homicide after allegedly firing his gun during a physical fight. Dean Plotts, 41, was charged with burglary with assault or battery. A St. Lucie County sheriff's deputy traveling in the area witnessed the incident and detained Kukielka.

The Port St. Lucie Police Department said the incident happened at about 6:30 p.m. near Southwest California Boulevard and Southwest Brevity Terrace. Before the shooting, one driver believed he was being followed after merging onto Southwest Crosstown Parkway. The vehicles had passed each other, and one driver believed the other had cut him off. Investigators determined there was no intentional following.

Kukielka was driving with his girlfriend to her home after leaving a local restaurant. Plotts was traveling in the same direction. The situation escalated into a physical fight near Southwest Brevity Terrace. During the fight, Kukielka allegedly fired his gun, striking Plotts twice in the left wrist and legs.

Plotts was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital for treatment. Kukielka was also taken to a hospital for a medical evaluation. Investigators recovered surveillance video and shell casings during the investigation. Both men were taken into custody. The incident remains under investigation.

hero.headline: Martin County High School receives third bomb threat in eight days
hero.body:
Martin County High School received another bomb threat Friday afternoon through the state's FortifyFL reporting system, the third threat involving the campus this week, the school district said.

The latest threat referenced two specific buildings, requiring students and staff to be evacuated while law enforcement conducted a thorough search. Students and staff were relocated to other areas of campus during the response.

Principal Lori Vogel warned families that the district has zero tolerance for false threats and that any individual found responsible will face severe school disciplinary consequences and potential criminal charges.

"Every threat must be taken seriously," Vogel said in a message to families. "Each report generates a significant law enforcement response, disrupts instruction, displaces students and staff, and creates understandable concern throughout our school community."

On Monday, students and staff were evacuated after a bomb threat prompted a response from the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Eight days ago, students and staff were evacuated in the afternoon after a bomb threat was received via email, according to school officials.

Vogel urged parents to speak directly with their children about the consequences of false threats.

"What a student may view as a joke or a temporary way to avoid class can have widespread consequences for an entire campus and community," Vogel said. "FortifyFL is an important safety resource. Students and families who become aware of a credible threat—or who have a legitimate reason to believe questionable, dangerous or criminal activity may be occurring—should continue to report that information through FortifyFL."

The principal's message emphasized that FortifyFL must never be used to submit information that someone knows to be false.

"We appreciate your partnership in reinforcing that false threats are neither harmless nor funny," Vogel said. "They place an unacceptable burden on students, employees, families, law enforcement and the broader community—and they must stop."

Information about submitting a report is available on the school's and the School District's websites.

cards.headline: Martin County issues blue-green algae alert for Lake Okeechobee area at J&S Fish Camp
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Health in Martin County issued a health alert after water samples detected harmful toxins in blue-green algae at the Lake Okeechobee NES135 area.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Health in Martin County issued a blue-green algae health alert for the Lake Okeechobee NES135 area after water samples detected harmful toxins. The alert covers an area on the north shore of the lake at J&S Fish Camp in Martin County and was issued in response to samples collected in September.

Residents and visitors should not drink, swim, wade, use personal watercraft or otherwise come into contact with water where a visible algae bloom is present. Health officials advised people to keep pets and livestock away from affected water. Anyone who comes into contact with algae, discolored water or water with an unpleasant odor should wash their skin and clothing with soap and water. Contaminated water should not be used for cooking or washing dishes because boiling does not remove algae toxins.

Blue-green algae are bacteria commonly found in Florida freshwater. Blooms can discolor water and create floating mats, scum, foam or paint-like material on the surface, sometimes with an unpleasant odor. The blooms can produce toxins that may harm people, pets and aquatic life. Children, older adults and people with weakened immune systems may be at risk even at low toxin concentrations and should avoid exposure.

It is safe to eat fillets from healthy freshwater fish caught in lakes experiencing blooms if the fillets are rinsed with tap or bottled water, the guts are discarded and the fish is thoroughly cooked. People should not eat shellfish from waters with algae blooms. The Florida Department of Environmental Protection monitors reported blooms and collects samples for analysis. The public can report an algae bloom online at ReportAlgalBloom.com or call 1-855-305-3903. Anyone who develops symptoms after exposure can call the Florida Poison Information Center at 800-222-1222. Pet owners who believe an animal became ill after exposure should contact a veterinarian. For health questions about blue-green algae, call DOH-Martin at 772-221-4090.

hero.headline: DeSantis sets Oct. 20 execution for William Reaves Jr. in 1986 Indian River County deputy murder
hero.body:
Governor Ron DeSantis has signed a death warrant for William Reaves Jr., setting an execution date of Oct. 20 for the 77-year-old man convicted of murdering Indian River County Sheriff's Deputy Richard Raczkoski in 1986. The execution is scheduled for 6 p.m. at Florida State Prison in Raiford, 40 years after the deputy's death.

Deputy Raczkoski was killed on Sept. 23, 1986, after responding to a 911 call at a convenience store. During a conversation with Reaves, a gun fell from Reaves's shorts. Deputy Raczkoski placed his knee on the weapon. Reaves then pushed the deputy away, grabbed the gun and pointed it at Deputy Raczkoski's face. As Deputy Raczkoski attempted to draw his own weapon, Reaves said, "I wouldn't do that if I were you." The deputy backed away, turned, and ran. Reaves fired seven rounds, striking Deputy Raczkoski four times.

Reaves was tried in the 19th Judicial Circuit in Indian River County. The Florida Supreme Court reversed the initial conviction and remanded the case for a new trial. On remand, Reaves was again convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death on March 6, 1992, in Vero Beach. The Florida Supreme Court affirmed the conviction and death sentence on April 7, 1994. The United States Supreme Court denied Reaves's petition for a writ of certiorari on Nov. 7, 1994.

Reaves pursued numerous postconviction challenges in both state and federal courts over the following decades. In 2015, the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida granted Reaves's federal petition for a writ of habeas corpus. The Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit overturned that ruling and ordered that the petition be denied. Additional postconviction motions and petitions were subsequently denied, and those denials were affirmed on appeal. Executive clemency was also considered and denied.

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier, in his letter recommending the warrant, wrote that "the record is legally sufficient to support the issuance of a death warrant," and confirmed that "there are no stays of execution issued by any court of competent jurisdiction in this cause."

cards.teaser: Two Sebastian police officers are on administrative leave after fatally shooting Keaton Daucher, 41, who emerged from a home with a shotgun during a noise complaint call Thursday night. The Florida Department of Law Enforcement is investigating.
cards.body:
Two Sebastian police officers have been placed on paid administrative leave after fatally shooting a 41-year-old man who emerged from a home with a shotgun Thursday night in the 500 block of Joy Haven Drive.

Daucher then came out of the home with a shotgun, prompting the two officers to discharge their weapons, killing him. Police said it was unclear if Daucher, who lived at the home, pointed the shotgun at the officers or if he fired any shots.

Law enforcement had previously been at the house before Thursday. The investigation has been turned over to the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, which is standard practice for the Sebastian Police Department.

Neither of the officers were hurt. Both remain on paid administrative leave pending the investigation.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie MRI technician arrested on felony sexual battery charge

cards.headline: Free Responsible Dog Ownership Day in Fort Pierce Saturday aims to ease shelter overcrowding
cards.teaser: The Treasure Coast Kennel Club and Dogs and Cats Forever Animal Sanctuary are hosting a free event Saturday at 9 a.m. to educate families about responsible pet ownership and support overcrowded local shelters.
cards.body:
The Treasure Coast Kennel Club and Dogs and Cats Forever Animal Sanctuary are hosting a free Responsible Dog Ownership Day on Saturday at 9 a.m. at Dogs and Cats Forever Animal Sanctuary, located at 4600 Selvitz Road in Fort Pierce. The event aims to educate pet owners about training and care while raising support for shelter animals as local rescues deal with overcrowding and supply shortages.

Susan Lyons with the Treasure Coast Kennel Club said the event is designed to help reduce shelter returns. "It's a free event so that people can come out and get information about how to be responsible dog owners so that we don't see dogs being returned to the shelter," Lyons said.

The event will feature dog training demonstrations, agility showcases, therapy and service dog education, raffles, food trucks and activities for children including bounce houses and a scavenger hunt. The Fort Pierce canine unit will conduct a demonstration. Families who participate in the scavenger hunt can collect vouchers from vendors to receive a free raffle ticket. Raffle prizes include gift baskets, gift cards, and a television.

Dogs available for future adoption through Dogs and Cats Forever Animal Sanctuary will be featured during the event, including Libby, a 9-year-old terrier. Nancy Dunn of Dogs and Cats Forever Animal Sanctuary said the first 50 people who bring a donation will receive swag bags. "Things that we need are dog food, cat food, flat sheets right now for puppies, blankets, towels — those kinds of things we're always in need of," Dunn said. Organizers encourage attendees to bring unopened pet food, towels, blankets, or other donation items to support the shelter.

hero.headline: Indian River County sex sting nets 50 arrests, child-luring case highlighted
hero.body:
Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers announced Thursday that law enforcement made 50 arrests during a four-day operation called Operation Late Checkout that targeted human trafficking. Nearly all the arrests were for prostitution. Investigators also identified multiple individuals they believe are victims of human trafficking, and those investigations are ongoing.

Flowers said the operation specifically targeted the trafficking of children and worked to capture people trying to lure children on the internet and meet up with them. Authorities pointed to the case of Carlos Reyes-Ayala, who is accused of traveling to Indian River County to meet with a child for sex.

Flowers said investigators connected with many others seeking to exploit children during the operation. "We had a whole roomful of detectives that were chatting undercover with people who wanted to meet up with children. Our team was busy for days," Flowers said.

Operation Late Checkout involved local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies. "This operation shows that within our communities, there are dangerous individuals committing heinous crimes who think they can get away with it," said Special Agent Alphonso Williams of the Florida Department of Law Enforcement.

Flowers said he expects more arrests to happen as a result of Operation Late Checkout. "It hurts our hearts when we see these cases and we see these kids. So, that's why we do these things," Flowers said.

hero.headline: Trail camera captures Florida panther mother with three cubs near Fort Myers
hero.body:
A trail camera at a nature reserve in Fort Myers has captured new footage of a Florida panther mother with three young cubs, offering a promising sign for the endangered species' recovery. The sighting is significant because it occurred farther north than where the endangered cats are usually seen in the state.

Experts say the footage indicates the panthers are expanding their breeding range, which could help the population recover. Florida panthers are an isolated population of the North American cougar, a species of large, solitary wild cats that range mostly in western North America and most of South America. There are thought to be some 200 individuals living in southern Florida.

Florida has spent decades trying to protect its panthers, primarily from encounters with cars and from a shrinking natural habitat. The cats' natural habitat has been reduced by about 95 percent from its original expanse.

The trail camera video shows the mother and three young cubs moving through the Fort Myers nature reserve. The expansion of the breeding range north of their typical territory represents a potential turning point for a species that has faced severe population pressures from both vehicle collisions and habitat loss throughout southern Florida.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie police arrest travel MRI technician on felony sexual battery charge
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police arrested Gabriel Cruz, a 42-year-old MRI technician, on charges of felony sexual battery after a 64-year-old female patient reported being assaulted during an MRI procedure at HCA Florida St. Lucie Hospital. The arrest followed an investigation that included video evidence from the hospital and forensic testing that returned presumptive positive results for the presence of male semen.

Detectives responded to the hospital at 1800 SE Tiffany Ave. on Sept. 14, 2026, after staff reported that the patient disclosed she was sexually assaulted while undergoing an MRI the previous day. The victim had been admitted for medical treatment and was administered medication that caused her to become significantly drowsy prior to the procedure. Cruz was identified as the MRI technician assigned to the procedure.

Video evidence obtained with the hospital's assistance showed Cruz exiting the MRI room after the victim and disposing of materials that were later secured by law enforcement. Testing of the materials returned presumptive positive results for the presence of male semen. Detectives confirmed Cruz had been working at the hospital as a travel MRI technician since Aug. 24, 2026, and was hired through a third-party agency.

Detectives determined there was probable cause to charge Cruz with sexual battery, a first-degree felony under Florida Statute 794.011(4)(b), involving a victim who was physically helpless or incapacitated. Cruz was arrested in Brevard County on the evening of Sept. 16, 2026. The investigation remains active and ongoing.

HCA Florida St. Lucie Hospital cooperated fully with law enforcement throughout the investigation. In a statement, the hospital said it does not tolerate behavior that jeopardizes the safety or security of patients. When the allegation was reported, the hospital contacted law enforcement and ended Cruz's assignment. The hospital said it has assisted law enforcement throughout its investigation and remains focused on supporting the patient.

The Port St. Lucie Police Department reminded the community to report incidents of sexual assault immediately to law enforcement or trusted resources. Such reports can ensure victims receive support and allow law enforcement to investigate. Cruz is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in a court of law.

hero.headline: Indian River County sex sting nets 50+ arrests, child-luring case
hero.body:
More than 50 people were arrested in a multi-agency operation targeting human trafficking and illegal sexual activity in Indian River County, including a man who traveled to meet a minor. Sheriff Eric Flowers announced the results of Operation Late Checkout during a press conference Thursday alongside a representative from the Florida Department of Law Enforcement.

The operation ran from Sept. 13 and netted over 60 contacts, more than 50 arrests, and three ICE detainers, Flowers said. One case involved a man who traveled to Indian River County to meet a minor. Flowers said the arrest was the result of the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force working across agencies to apprehend individuals attempting to lure children online.

Agencies involved in the operation included the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Florida Department of Law Enforcement, St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Seminole County Sheriff's Office, Altamonte Springs Police Department, Vero Beach Police Department, Homeland Security Investigations, Florida Office of Statewide Prosecutor and the U.S. Attorney's Office. During the operation, several victims were identified, and ongoing investigations are underway. Flowers said there are no specific arrests on human trafficking charges at this time.

Flowers called the operation unprecedented for Indian River County. "We've never had an investigation like this, to my knowledge, in Indian River County with this many agencies involved, with this many arrests in one shot," he said. FDLE Assistant Special Agent in Charge Alfonso Williams said Operation Late Checkout was initiated by FDLE in coordination with the Indian River County Sheriff's Office and is the first operation of this magnitude conducted in the county.

Undercover teams were deployed in a variety of capacities during the operation. Victims' advocates trained to work with trafficking victims were also on hand to speak with women involved in prostitution to determine whether they were being trafficked. "We have many ongoing investigations as a result of this," Flowers said. Williams said the operation focused on identifying human trafficking victims, reducing the demand for prostitution, and apprehending individuals seeking sexual contact with minors. Anyone who suspects someone is a victim of trafficking can contact the Florida Trafficking Hotline at 1-855-352-7233.

cards.headline: Vero Beach police officer on paid leave after alleged misuse of Flock system
cards.teaser: The Vero Beach Police Department has placed an officer on administrative leave with pay amid an investigation into alleged misuse of the Flock Safety license plate reader system.
cards.body:
The Vero Beach Police Department has placed an officer on administrative leave with pay amid an investigation into alleged misuse of the Flock Safety license plate reader system. The department launched the investigation after being contacted by a news organization.

"The Vero Beach Police Department remains committed to accountability, transparency, and ensuring that law enforcement technology is used only for legitimate and authorized purposes," the department said in a statement. The department said no additional information will be released while the investigation is active.

The investigation comes as several local municipalities are restricting the use of automated license plate readers such as Flock. A former Fort Pierce police officer was recently accused of misusing law enforcement databases to track his ex-girlfriend. His court case is pending.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Regional Airport approves 500-space paid parking lot, ending free parking
cards.teaser: Vero Beach City Council approved construction of a new long-term parking lot that will expand capacity from 80 spaces to over 500 at Vero Beach Regional Airport, ending free parking as officials cite rising flight demand.
cards.body:
Vero Beach City Council approved construction of a new long-term parking lot that will expand capacity from 80 spaces to over 500 at Vero Beach Regional Airport, ending free parking as officials cite rising flight demand and the airport's self-funding model.

Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the expansion is driven by new flights coming to the airport. The current parking situation is not keeping up, Dambeck said, and the grass parking area looks disorganized. The airport operates without taxpayer dollars and must use the funds to cover the costs of any upgrades to the airport, Dambeck said.

Envision Parking Partners will build and pay for the lot. The airport will be responsible for maintaining it. John Mostoller with Envision said travelers will be able to pay through a prepaid option using license plate readers or at the lot gate. The new lot will also add cameras and lighting for security. No parking spot will be more than two to four minutes from the terminal, Mostoller said.

Some travelers said they will miss the free parking. Traveler Reana Tejada said that sucks and that free parking was a nice plus. Sydney Banak, who was able to park for free during her visit, said she understands the reasoning behind the change. Free parking is nice, Sydney said, but maybe they need to expand the airport or provide more services.

Construction is expected to begin in March and be completed by next summer. The airport previously announced upgrades including new covered walkways and baggage claim, and a new patio.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce planning board delays decision on Willow Lakes data center rezoning
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce's planning board delayed a decision on rezoning 200 acres near Interstate 95 and Midway Road for a data center after residents expressed divided opinions on environmental impact and job creation.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce's planning board delayed a decision on a proposal to rezone 200 acres near Interstate 95 and Midway Road for a data center and commercial development after residents expressed mixed reactions. The board requested the planning department conduct further research and asked the city to discuss the item at the next commission meeting.

The property, currently zoned for a mixed-use development called Willow Lakes, would be partially rezoned under the proposal. About 174 acres would be designated for light industrial use limited to data center operations, while the remaining 26 acres along Midway Road would be rezoned for general commercial use, potentially allowing for a hotel, gas station, restaurants or retail businesses.

The planning board did not decide whether a data center qualifies as a permitted use within the light industrial zoning category. The applicant, Willow Lakes LLC, tabled the rezoning application as a result. W. Lee Dobbins, the attorney representing Willow Lakes LLC, said there is no point in moving forward with rezoning to light industrial until the city makes a decision on the code. Willow Lakes LLC emphasized the site's access to significant electrical infrastructure, including Florida Power Light transmission lines and a nearby substation. A large man-made lake on the property could serve as a water source for the data center's cooling system.

Residents expressed divided opinions about the proposal. Sarah Quinette said residents are not OK with a data center built next to their homes. She said keeping the area as agricultural land has a great impact in the form of pollinating insects that will return season after season. Felix Rodriguez said he thinks the project is cool because it brings in more jobs, construction and trade work, and the freight brings in more business. Shirley McHellon voiced opposition, saying the city needs to stop taking away the trees, woods and animals.

Before the data center can move forward with approval, the city must first decide whether to approve the rezoning request. Further research is required before the planning board revisits the proposal.

The property, currently zoned for a mixed-use development called "Willow Lakes," would be partially rezoned under the proposal. About 174 acres would be designated for light industrial use, limited to data center operations, while the remaining 26 acres along Midway Road would be rezoned for general commercial use, potentially allowing for a hotel, gas station, restaurants or retail businesses. The applicant, Willow Lakes LLC, emphasized the site’s access to significant electrical infrastructure, including Florida Power Light transmission lines and a nearby substation. A large man-made lake on the property could also serve as a water source for the data center’s cooling system. During the meeting, the planning board made two motions. The first requested the planning department to conduct further research on the data center proposal and report back. The second motion called for the city to discuss the item at the next commission meeting. As a result, the board did not decide whether a data center qualifies as a permitted use within the light industrial zoning category, prompting the applicant to table the rezoning application. "Therefore, there is no point in us moving forward with rezoning to light industrial," said W. Lee Dobbins, the attorney representing Willow Lakes LLC. "We would need to wait until that decision is over and make a decision at that time based upon what they changed the code to say." Residents expressed a range of opinions about the proposal. "We're not OK with them building a data center right next to our homes," said resident Sarah Quinette. "An area like that, if we keep it as agricultural land, it has a great impact in the form of pollinating insects that will return season after season." Felix Rodriguez, another resident, shared a different perspective. "I think it's pretty cool personally, just because it brings in more jobs, construction, that trade. All the freight just brings in more business," he said. Shirley McHellon voiced her opposition to the project. "I think they need to stop. They're taking away the trees, the woods and the animals ... they're just killing the animals," she said. Before the data center can move forward with approval, the city must first decide whether to approve the rezoning request. hero.headline: Martin County approves limited-industrial zoning for Hobe Sound property in 3-2 vote
hero.body:
Martin County commissioners voted 3-2 Tuesday to rezone a property along Southeast Powerline Avenue in Hobe Sound to limited-industrial, a compromise that stepped back from a general industrial designation that drew pushback from nearby residents. Commissioner Blake Capps voted against the rezoning, citing concerns about the potential for a data center on the site.

The property has long been slated for some form of industrial use, but the county said the existing zoning was outdated and due for an update. After hearing from residents who opposed the general industrial classification, the property owner offered to accept the less-intensive limited-industrial designation.

Bob Reins, a land-use attorney with Gunster law firm representing the property owner, told commissioners his client was willing to accept the light industrial classification if that was what neighbors felt was more appropriate. Capps said he remained opposed even to the compromise. "Who knows where this is really going in the future and to approve a zoning for this property that allows a data center. I'm not into that," Capps said.

Residents who spoke at the commission meeting said their primary concern was protecting the character of the community. Steve Addison, who has lived in the area since 1969, said his biggest concern was preserving quality of life. "We don't have a lot of industry and a lot of noise," Addison said. Kim Call, a resident, said growth needs to be compatible with the community that already exists. Patrick McDonough, a Hobe Sound resident and Eaglewood Community HOA president, said residents were concerned about the permanence of a general industrial classification which they believed was too broad and too open-ended.

The county said there are no plans for a data center at the site. Any proposal exceeding 100,000 square feet would require board approval. Addison said after the vote he felt the compromise was the right move. "I don't want to see over development, but I also don't want to be that guy that doesn't understand land-use and doesn't understand property rights," Addison said. "I feel like it was a win win for the both of us."

hero.headline: Florida requires parental opt-in for AI classroom tools by July 1, 2027
hero.body:
Parents will have to give permission before public and charter school students in Florida use artificial intelligence instructional tools under rules approved Wednesday by the State Board of Education.

Public school districts and charter schools have until July 1, 2027, to adopt and implement policies requiring parental opt-in. Students whose families decline must receive a comparable alternative without AI. The rules prohibit instructional chatbots designed to simulate friendship or emotional relationships with students, undisclosed psychological profiling and vendors selling student data.

Schools must notify parents when an AI instructional tool is approved, including which tool students would use, the courses involved and how students would interact with it. Tools used with children in pre-kindergarten through fifth grade face additional review for age and developmental appropriateness.

Gov. Ron DeSantis promoted the requirements during a Thursday appearance in Melbourne, saying technology should supplement classroom instruction. "We are not going to be displacing a classroom teacher with machines," DeSantis said. "We're going to continue to value the human experience in education, and not sacrifice that at the altar of technology."

Education Commissioner Henry Mack said the concern is whether students are developing their own understanding when they turn to AI for answers. "So if a course is designed to cultivate critical thinking, we do not want AI doing that on behalf of the learner," Mack said.

The board also approved rules for Florida College System institutions. Their policies must prohibit students from using AI on graded assignments or tests unless an instructor explicitly authorizes it.

Florida Education Association Vice President Carole Gauronskas expressed support for the policies overall while questioning how much additional work implementation could create for school districts. "We encourage this board to convene a panel of experts, including parents, guardians, and come up with more guidance and guardrails just to make sure that that human touch is there," she said.

Teachers and administrators will also need training on AI's risks, limitations, safety and compliance requirements. Many districts already have AI policies but will need to align them with the new statewide requirements. Mack said the Department of Education would organize work groups, coordinate with superintendents and provide resources to help carry out the rules.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie hospital MRI technician arrested for felony sexual battery of patient
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police arrested Gabriel Cruz, a 42-year-old MRI technician, on charges of felony sexual battery after a 64-year-old female patient reported being assaulted during an MRI procedure at HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital.

On September 14, 2026, detectives responded to the hospital, located at 1800 SE Tiffany Ave., after staff reported that the patient disclosed she was sexually assaulted while undergoing an MRI the previous day. The victim had been admitted for medical treatment and was administered medication that caused her to become significantly drowsy prior to the procedure. Cruz was identified as the MRI technician assigned to the procedure.

Video evidence obtained with the hospital's assistance showed Cruz exiting the MRI room after the victim and disposing of materials that were later secured by law enforcement. Testing of the materials returned presumptive positive results for the presence of male semen. Detectives confirmed Cruz had been working at the hospital as a travel MRI technician since August 24, 2026, and was hired through a third-party agency.

Following the review of evidence, detectives determined there was probable cause to charge Cruz with sexual battery, a first-degree felony under Florida Statute 794.011(4)(b), involving a victim who was physically helpless or incapacitated. Cruz was arrested in Brevard County on the evening of September 16, 2026, in connection with the investigation. The investigation remains active and ongoing.

HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital has cooperated fully with law enforcement throughout the investigation. In a statement, the hospital said it does not tolerate behavior that jeopardizes the safety or security of patients. When the allegation was reported, the hospital contacted law enforcement and ended Cruz's assignment. The hospital said it has assisted law enforcement throughout its investigation and remains focused on supporting the patient.

The Port St. Lucie Police Department reminded the community to report incidents of sexual assault immediately to law enforcement or trusted resources, emphasizing that such reports can ensure victims receive support and allow law enforcement to investigate. Cruz is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in a court of law.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie police arrest fentanyl dealer after texting him from overdose victim's phone
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police arrested a man on fentanyl trafficking charges after investigators used a fatal overdose victim's phone to arrange a drug buy, leading to a search that turned up guns, drugs, and more than $17,000 in cash.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police arrested a man on fentanyl trafficking charges after investigators used a fatal overdose victim's phone to arrange a drug buy, leading to a search that turned up guns, drugs, and more than $17,000 in cash.

Officers responded to an apartment at 700 SE Collins Lane on September 13 for an overdose. They found 34-year-old Miqueias Oliveira Silva dead, with a bloody syringe and a bag of cocaine next to him. The arrest affidavit says rigor mortis suggested Silva had been dead for about 24 hours.

Investigators went through Silva's phone and found months of text exchanges with a contact saved under the name Danilo Jaramillo, going back to August 17. The affidavit says the messages followed a pattern, with Silva asking if Jaramillo was available and Jaramillo confirming before the two met up. Police used Silva's phone to text Jaramillo and arrange another deal. Jaramillo responded he could be there within the hour.

Investigators followed Jaramillo's black Kia Telluride to Silva's apartment complex and pulled him over. A K9 alerted to narcotics inside the vehicle. Investigators say they found a bag of fentanyl on the passenger seat, along with a large amount of cash.

Detectives then obtained a search warrant for Jaramillo's home on SW Longfellow Road. According to a separate affidavit, investigators searched the master bedroom and found three firearms: a Smith & Wesson .40 caliber handgun, a Ruger LC9 and an AR-15. They also found ammunition, digital scales, a written ledger, cocaine, marijuana and $17,715 in cash.

Jaramillo's wife, Selina Jaramillo, was home with their children during the search. According to the affidavit, she told investigators she didn't know he was involved in drugs and said she'd last seen him with narcotics about eight months earlier. She said one of the firearms was hers, but that the rest, along with the drugs and cash, belonged to her husband.

The affidavit says Jaramillo told police anything illegal in the home belonged to him, then asked for a lawyer before answering further questions. Because Jaramillo is a convicted felon, investigators charged him with three counts of possessing a firearm or ammunition as a felon.

Jaramillo, 43, faces multiple felony drug charges, including fentanyl trafficking, along with three felony weapons counts and a misdemeanor paraphernalia charge. Police say body cameras were active throughout the search and the footage was submitted into evidence.

Magalys Koch, a substance abuse expert at Hibiscus Counseling, said the pain is felt not just by victims and dealers, but by the people around them. Many parents or family members feel guilty, like they didn't do enough or they couldn't, Koch said.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce planning board delays data center rezoning at I-95 and Midway Road
hero.body:
The Fort Pierce planning board delayed a decision on a proposal to rezone 200 acres near Interstate 95 and Midway Road for a data center and commercial development, requesting further research before the matter moves to the city commission.

The board made two motions at its meeting. The first requested the planning department to conduct further research on the data center proposal and report back. The second motion called for the city to discuss the item at the next commission meeting. The board did not decide whether a data center qualifies as a permitted use within the light industrial zoning category, prompting the applicant to table the rezoning application.

The property, currently zoned for a mixed-use development called Willow Lakes, would be partially rezoned under the proposal submitted by Willow Lakes LLC. About 174 acres would be designated for light industrial use, limited to data center operations, while the remaining 26 acres along Midway Road would be rezoned for general commercial use, potentially allowing for a hotel, gas station, restaurants or retail businesses.

W. Lee Dobbins, the attorney representing Willow Lakes LLC, said the applicant would wait for the city to resolve the code definition question. "Therefore, there is no point in us moving forward with rezoning to light industrial," Dobbins said. "We would need to wait until that decision is over and make a decision at that time based upon what they changed the code to say."

The applicant emphasized the site's access to significant electrical infrastructure, including Florida Power Light transmission lines and a nearby substation. A large man-made lake on the property could also serve as a water source for the data center's cooling system.

Residents expressed divided opinions about the proposal. "We're not OK with them building a data center right next to our homes," said resident Sarah Quinette. "An area like that, if we keep it as agricultural land, it has a great impact in the form of pollinating insects that will return season after season."

Felix Rodriguez offered a different perspective. "I think it's pretty cool personally, just because it brings in more jobs, construction, that trade. All the freight just brings in more business," he said.

Shirley McHellon voiced opposition to the project. "I think they need to stop. They're taking away the trees, the woods and the animals ... they're just killing the animals," she said.

Before the data center can move forward with approval, the city must first decide whether to approve the rezoning request.

cards.headline: Vero Beach City Council approves 500-space paid parking lot at Regional Airport
cards.teaser: Vero Beach Regional Airport will replace free parking with a paid 500-space lot as the airport funds upgrades ahead of new flight service. Construction begins in March.
cards.body:
Vero Beach City Council approved construction of a new long-term parking lot at Vero Beach Regional Airport that will expand capacity from 80 spaces to over 500 spaces and end free parking at the facility.

Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the expansion is driven by new flights coming to the airport. The current parking situation is not keeping up, Dambeck said, noting the grass parking area looks disorganized. The airport operates without taxpayer dollars and must use the funds to cover the costs of upgrades to the airport.

"The airport is responsible for maintaining its self-sustainability, meaning we don't take any taxpayer dollars," Dambeck said. "We have to make sure that our charges will help to to maintain the operations that happen at the airport."

Envision Parking Partners will build and pay for the lot. The airport will be responsible for maintaining it. John Mostoller with Envision said travelers will be able to pay through a prepaid option using license plate readers or at the lot gate. The new lot will also add cameras and lighting for security. No parking spot will be more than two to four minutes from the terminal, Mostoller said.

Traveler Reana Tejada said she will miss the free parking. "That sucks. I mean, that's — it's a nice plus to be able to park, especially if it was already free," Tejada said.

Sydney Banak, who was able to park for free during her visit, said she understands the reasoning behind the change. "Free parking is nice," Sydney said. "But maybe they need to expand the airport or provide more services, so I do understand where they're coming from with that."

Construction is expected to begin in March and be completed by next summer. The airport is also adding new covered walkways and baggage claim, and a new patio.

cards.headline: Travel MRI technician arrested on sexual battery charge at HCA Florida St. Lucie Hospital
cards.teaser: Gabriel Cruz, 42, was arrested on a first-degree felony charge after a sedated 64-year-old patient reported an assault during an MRI procedure at the Port St. Lucie hospital.
cards.body:
Gabriel Cruz, a 42-year-old travel MRI technician, was arrested on a first-degree felony sexual battery charge after a sedated patient reported an assault at HCA Florida St. Lucie Hospital in Port St. Lucie. Port St. Lucie police arrested Cruz in Brevard County on the evening of Sept. 16.

The investigation began Sept. 14 after hospital staff reported that a 64-year-old female patient said she had been sexually assaulted during an MRI the day before at the hospital at 1800 SE Tiffany Ave. The woman had been admitted for medical treatment and was given medication before the MRI that left her significantly drowsy, police said.

Detectives identified Cruz as the technician assigned to the procedure. With the hospital's assistance, investigators obtained video that police said showed Cruz leaving the MRI room after the patient and disposing of materials. Those materials were recovered and tested, returning presumptive positive results for male semen, according to police.

Cruz had worked at the hospital as a travel MRI technician since Aug. 24 and was hired through a third-party agency, police said. The charge is sexual battery involving a physically helpless or incapacitated victim. The investigation remains active.

HCA Florida St. Lucie Hospital cooperated with investigators, police said. In a statement, the hospital said it does not tolerate behavior that jeopardizes the safety or security of patients. The hospital said it contacted law enforcement when the allegation was reported and ended Cruz's assignment. The hospital said it has assisted law enforcement throughout the investigation and remains focused on supporting the patient.

Small Craft Advisories will activate this afternoon for boaters along the coast. The northeast flow creating the flood risk will also generate rough conditions on local waters.

Conditions will remain partly cloudy between the rain bands, with high temperatures reaching the upper 80s. The streaming showers are expected to continue as long as the northeast wind pattern persists.

The advisories reflect the combination of persistent moisture moving onshore and gusty winds that will affect both land and marine areas through the afternoon hours.

hero.headline: Indian River County sheriff announces 50+ arrests in multi-agency human trafficking operation
hero.body:
Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers announced more than 50 arrests following a multi-agency, multi-day operation targeting human trafficking and illegal sexual activity in the county. Operation Late Checkout ran from Sept. 13 and netted over 60 contacts, more than 50 arrests, and three ICE detainers. The operation also resulted in a child-luring case in which a man traveled to Indian River County to meet a minor.

Flowers said during a Thursday press conference that several victims were identified during the operation, and ongoing investigations are underway. Victims' advocates trained to work with trafficking victims were on hand to speak with women involved in prostitution to determine whether they were being trafficked. There are no specific arrests on human trafficking charges at this time, Flowers said.

Flowers called the operation unprecedented for Indian River County. "We've never had an investigation like this, to my knowledge, in Indian River County with this many agencies involved, with this many arrests in one shot," he said. FDLE Assistant Special Agent in Charge Alfonso Williams said Operation Late Checkout was initiated by FDLE in coordination with the Indian River County Sheriff's Office and is the first operation of this magnitude conducted in the county.

Agencies involved in the operation included the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Florida Department of Law Enforcement, St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Seminole County Sheriff's Office, Altamonte Springs Police Department, Vero Beach Police Department, Homeland Security Investigations, Florida Office of Statewide Prosecutor and the U.S. Attorney's Office. Undercover teams were deployed in a variety of capacities during the operation. The child-luring arrest was the result of the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force working across agencies to apprehend individuals attempting to lure children online. "Our team did a great job of getting him off the street," Flowers said.

Williams said the operation focused on identifying human trafficking victims, reducing the demand for prostitution, and apprehending individuals seeking sexual contact with minors. "Our work is far from done," Williams said. "This operation requires a lot of resources and time. We cannot do this work alone, and our success depends on the great partnership and collaboration that you see today." FDLE houses the Florida Trafficking Hotline. Anyone who suspects someone is a victim of trafficking can contact the hotline at 1-855-352-7233.

cards.headline: Vero Beach animal hospital manager arrested for abandoning cats after reclaiming them from Humane Society
cards.teaser: Deanna Rae Wesley, 43, a manager at Dr. Dan's Animal Hospital in Vero Beach, faces two counts of animal abandonment after investigators said she picked up two cats from the Humane Society and left them outside without care.
cards.body:
Deanna Rae Wesley, 43, a manager at Dr. Dan's Animal Hospital in Vero Beach, was arrested Sept. 15 on two counts of animal abandonment after investigators said she reclaimed two cats from the Humane Society of Vero Beach and Indian River County and then abandoned them outdoors without care. A judge set bond at $250 per count, for a total of $500, according to Indian River County court records.

Animal Control investigators said Wesley picked up two white-and-brown tabby cats from the Humane Society on Sept. 8. Wesley told staff the cats were being returned to a caregiver but would not identify that person, the affidavit said.

The next day, Animal Control received a complaint about a white-and-brown tabby cat crying at a resident's front door. The cat was taken to Animal Control, where its microchip and Humane Society staff confirmed it was one of the cats Wesley had picked up. Wesley initially denied it was the same cat but acknowledged the matching microchip number, according to investigators. She declined to explain how the cat ended up loose at the home, the affidavit said.

The resident told investigators that a woman matching Wesley's description, wearing a Dr. Dan's T-shirt, spoke with her mother and warned her to watch out for Animal Control in the area. The woman allegedly called the cats colony cats, the affidavit said.

Animal Control recovered the second cat at the same residence Sept. 10. Both cats were described as extremely friendly, with debris on their faces and chins. Investigators said the cats were not capable of surviving outdoors on their own and that no one was known to be caring for them. The warrant alleges Wesley abandoned the cats on a public street without providing care, food, protection or shelter.

hero.headline: Travel MRI technician arrested on sexual battery charge at HCA Florida St. Lucie Hospital
hero.body:
A 42-year-old travel MRI technician was arrested on a first-degree felony sexual battery charge after a sedated patient reported an assault at HCA Florida St. Lucie Hospital in Port St. Lucie.

Gabriel Cruz was arrested in Brevard County on the evening of Sept. 16 on a charge of sexual battery involving a physically helpless or incapacitated victim. Cruz had worked at the hospital at 1800 SE Tiffany Ave. as a travel MRI technician since Aug. 24 and was hired through a third-party agency, according to Port St. Lucie police.

The investigation began Sept. 14 after hospital staff reported that a 64-year-old female patient said she had been sexually assaulted during an MRI the day before. The woman had been admitted for medical treatment and was given medication before the MRI that left her significantly drowsy, police said.

Detectives identified Cruz as the technician assigned to the procedure. With the hospital's assistance, investigators obtained video that police said showed Cruz leaving the MRI room after the patient and disposing of materials. Those materials were recovered and tested, returning presumptive positive results for male semen, according to police.

HCA Florida St. Lucie Hospital has cooperated with investigators, police said. The investigation remains active.

cards.headline: Amazon shuts Port St. Lucie fulfillment center for $200 million robotics overhaul
cards.teaser: Amazon closed its Port St. Lucie fulfillment center Thursday for a renovation expected to last until 2028, with roughly 300 workers taking severance. The company plans to invest $200 million to add advanced robotics, artificial intelligence, and 870,000 square feet to the facility.
cards.body:
Amazon closed its Port St. Lucie fulfillment center Thursday for a major renovation expected to last until at least 2028, with the company investing about $200 million to add advanced robotics and artificial intelligence capabilities along with an additional 870,000 square feet. Around 300 employees are expected to take severance as the facility shuts down.

Amazon filed a layoff notice in July listing 494 affected employees. Workers who were employed at the facility before the closure will be eligible for rehire when it reopens, according to the Economic Development Council of St. Lucie County.

Local workforce organizations, including CareerSource Research Coast and the Economic Development Council of St. Lucie County, have spent recent months holding job fairs and helping affected workers connect with other employers. St. Lucie County Commissioner Cathy Townsend said the closure highlights the importance of attracting a wider range of businesses to the county.

"I think we need to be more strategic on the companies we want coming here," Townsend said. "My focus would be more on small businesses."

Amazon plans to reopen the facility in the second half of 2028 and hire more than 1,000 employees, according to the St. Lucie EDC. The closure is not expected to impact customers because operations will be handled by other facilities during the renovation, Amazon has said.

hero.headline: Indian River County sheriff announces 50+ arrests in multi-agency human trafficking operation
hero.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office announced more than 50 arrests following a multi-agency, multi-day operation targeting human trafficking and illegal sexual activity in the county. Operation Late Checkout ran from Sept. 13 in Indian River County and netted over 60 contacts, more than 50 arrests, and three ICE detainers, Sheriff Eric Flowers said during a press conference on Thursday. Flowers said there are no specific arrests on human trafficking charges at this time.

Agencies involved in the operation included the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Florida Department of Law Enforcement, St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Seminole County Sheriff's Office, Altamonte Springs Police Department, Vero Beach Police Department, Homeland Security Investigations, Florida Office of Statewide Prosecutor and the U.S. Attorney's Office, Flowers said. During the operation, several victims were identified, and investigators said ongoing investigations are underway.

One case involved a man who traveled to Indian River County to meet a minor. Flowers said the arrest was the result of the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force working across agencies to apprehend individuals attempting to lure children online. Undercover teams were deployed in a variety of capacities during the operation. Victims' advocates trained to work with trafficking victims were also on hand to speak with women involved in prostitution to determine whether they were being trafficked.

Flowers called the operation unprecedented for Indian River County. He said he has no knowledge of an investigation in Indian River County with this many agencies involved and this many arrests in one shot. FDLE Assistant Special Agent in Charge Alfonso Williams said Operation Late Checkout was initiated by FDLE in coordination with the Indian River County Sheriff's Office and is the first operation of this magnitude conducted in the county. Williams said the operation focused on identifying human trafficking victims, reducing the demand for prostitution, and apprehending individuals seeking sexual contact with minors. FDLE houses the Florida Trafficking Hotline. Anyone who suspects someone is a victim of trafficking can contact the hotline at 1-855-352-7233.

cards.headline: Liquor theft at Martin County Publix leads to high-speed chase into Palm Beach County
cards.teaser: A 24-year-old man faces theft and fleeing charges after stealing liquor bottles from a Publix and leading deputies on a pursuit that crossed county lines.
cards.body:
A 24-year-old man faces theft and fleeing charges after stealing liquor bottles from a Publix in Martin County and leading deputies on a pursuit that crossed into Palm Beach County. Derwyn Edwards stole several bottles of liquor from a Publix before deputies attempted to stop him, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office.

Edwards refused to pull over when a deputy caught up with his vehicle, investigators said. Video from the pursuit shows him speeding, running red lights and coming dangerously close to other drivers on the road, authorities said.

Sheriff's office air crews tracked Edwards as he continued driving into Palm Beach County, deputies said. The chase ended when Edwards was taken into custody.

Edwards is now charged with theft and fleeing police.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce grants King's Landing developers six-month extension after failed termination motion
hero.body:
Fort Pierce city commissioners voted 3-2 Monday night to grant developers of the King's Landing project a six-month extension to raise $15 million for the long-delayed mixed-use development near the downtown marina.

The vote came after Commissioner Chris Dzadovsky made a motion to terminate the development agreement, which failed. Dzadovsky expressed frustration with the seven-year timeline. "Well, it's been seven years. We should be well past this process. I was disappointed in the outcome for sure," Dzadovsky said.

The multi-million-dollar project is expected to include a Marriott hotel, restaurant, residential units, retail space, and a parking garage. Current developer Bill Ware with Live Oak Holdings attended the meeting and requested commissioners not hold his company accountable for delays prior to Live Oak being approved in the April 2025 third amendment. "I respectfully request that we not be held captive or accountable for this ten-year-plus period of time and prior to Live Oak being approved in the April of 2025 third amendment," Ware said. Ware committed to continuing monthly and quarterly email updates.

Commissioners agreed to move forward but instructed developers to formally document their default. "Our concerns need to be addressed in that document, or it's not going to get approved," Michael Broderick said. Dzadovsky expressed skepticism about the extension leading to progress. "Given the seven years' experience, I think six months from now we'll be back to where we started today, last night," Dzadovsky said. Developers now have 180 days to secure the funding and move the project forward.

hero.body:
The Martin County Commission approved rezoning a property along Southeast Powerline Avenue in Hobe Sound to limited-industrial in a 3-2 vote Tuesday, stepping back from a general industrial designation that drew pushback from nearby residents. Commissioner Blake Capps voted against the rezoning, citing concerns about the potential for a data center on the site, while residents remain divided over whether the compromise adequately protects the community.

The property has long been slated for some form of industrial use, but the county said the existing zoning was outdated and due for an update. After residents voiced concerns at the Tuesday commission meeting, the property owner offered to accept the less-intensive limited-industrial classification.

Steve Addison, who has lived in the area since 1969, said residents were focused on preserving quality of life. Kim Call, a resident, said she believes growth needs to be compatible with the community that already exists. Patrick McDonough, a Hobe Sound resident and Eaglewood Community HOA president, said residents were concerned about the permanence of a general industrial classification which they believe is too broad and too open-ended.

Bob Reins, a land-use attorney with Gunster law firm representing the property owner, said they were willing to accept the light industrial classification to cooperate with neighbors. Capps said he was not willing to approve zoning for the property that allows a data center. The county said there are no plans for a data center at the site. Any proposal exceeding 100,000 square feet would require board approval. Addison said he felt the compromise was a win for both sides.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce approves $10.1 million contract for police body cameras and AI tools
hero.body:
The Fort Pierce city commission on Monday voted unanimously 5-0 to approve a $10.1 million, decade-long contract with Axon Enterprise, Inc. for body cameras, Tasers, and artificial intelligence technology tools for the police department.

The contract runs for five years with an optional automatic renewal for another five years. The 10-year contract will cost Fort Pierce $10,139,037.87. The city will make annual payments of $999,000 during the first five years. If the renewal option is exercised, the city will pay Axon Enterprise $1,028,807.57 annually for the final five years.

Fort Pierce Police Department Chief David M. Smith described the package as Axon Enterprise's top-tier offering. The equipment includes Tasers, also known as stun guns, and body cameras that translate languages immediately for officers. An officer would speak in their language, and the body camera will relay the message to the subject in their language. Smith said prior to the vote that the technology "will absolutely be a force multiplier for us."

The Axon technology will also help officers with redaction of police reports. Redactions are used to prevent personal information, like Social Security numbers, from being made public. According to the commission agenda, the current Axon body cameras owned by the police department were at the end of their life and needed to be replaced. Axon Enterprise is in Scottsdale, Arizona.

hero.headline: Diver finds suspected WWII torpedo off Fort Pierce beach during lobster hunt
hero.body:
A diver searching for lobster off Fort Pierce beach last month discovered a suspected World War II-era torpedo, prompting a controlled detonation by the U.S. Navy on Tuesday.

Luke Neiman was diving with his father and a friend just south of the jetty when he spotted the unusual object. Neiman said he was near a large condominium building when he came across something on the seafloor that did not look like a reef.

"I couldn't really make out what it was, but I just knew it wasn't a reef, and I was kind of inspecting it, looking at it," Neiman said. "I'm like, this just looks different, you know, and then before I knew it, I'm like, this is a torpedo, because I could make out the end of it and it had a cone nose."

Neiman returned to the boat, told his father to mark the spot, and contacted the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission. The FWC alerted the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office bomb squad, and the U.S. Navy was then notified.

Navy Explosive Ordnance Disposal personnel conducted a controlled underwater detonation at the site on Tuesday afternoon, Sept. 15, 2026. Navy officials confirmed the operation in a statement, saying the personnel conducted a routine underwater ordnance disposal operation in the waters off St. Lucie County. The Navy identified the object as a suspected World War II-era munition.

Neiman reflected on the discovery with surprise. "Yeah, it just really blew my mind literally that I found a torpedo down here right where I catch a bunch of lobster and stuff!" he said.
